T0658.title: DEX
T0658.definition: A DEX is a blockchain protocol that matches or automatically executes digital-asset trades through smart contracts, usually without a centralized institution taking custody of user assets.
T0658.description: A DEX lets users connect self-custody wallets to smart contracts for token swaps, liquidity provision, or order matching, commonly through automated market makers or on-chain order books. It reduces centralized custody and single-party control but is not inherently anonymous or risk-free: transactions are usually public, while smart-contract flaws, malicious tokens, liquidity manipulation, and compromised front ends remain possible. Launderers may use permissionless swaps to complicate tracing across assets, although DEX protocols are also legitimate blockchain infrastructure.
T0658.usageExample: Investigators found that illicit funds entered a DEX, were swapped through several tokens, and then dispersed to new addresses through a cross-chain bridge.
